workflows.title: Bug-Fix Loop (for lab / hands coding work)
workflows.body:
1. **REPRODUCE** — Capture the failure with a minimal trigger. No fix attempts
   until the failure is reproducible on demand.
2. **INSPECT** — Memory-first (T-06): search confirmed fixes for this error
   signature. If found, apply and go to VERIFY.
3. **FIX** — Smallest change that addresses the root cause, not the symptom.
4. **TEST** — Run the acceptance test that reproduces the failure.
5. **VERIFY** — Passing test + no regressions in neighboring tests.
6. **RECORD** — Store failure → fix → verified outcome (P-04). Unconfirmed
   attempts are discarded.
7. **PATCH** — Deliver the change with the test evidence attached.

workflows.title: Research Synthesis (deep-research pattern)
workflows.body:
1. **SCOPE** — Write the exact questions to answer; list what would disprove
   each candidate answer.
2. **COLLECT** — Gather from multiple independent sources; record source +
   date for every fact.
3. **CROSS-CHECK** — Facts appearing in only one source are marked unverified.
   Vendor claims are marked vendor-reported until independently confirmed
   (the ARC-AGI-3 lesson: 99.9% claimed vs 62.7% independent).
4. **SYNTHESIZE** — Answer each question with: finding, confidence, sources,
   what remains unknown.
5. **FILE** — Write to the knowledge pack with the Persian summary header.

techniques.title: Surgical Single-Word Regeneration
techniques.what_it_does: Drama 3 can reportedly fix a single word without regenerating the rest of a take — re-render only the bad word and drop it into the existing audio.
techniques.why_it_works: Full re-renders are expensive (compute + new seams + new QC surface). If the tokenizer boundary is clean and the acoustic context is re-supplied, a one-word patch is both cheaper and more consistent than a full take.
techniques.genesis_implementation: Build the render pipeline so every utterance keeps its token stream + reference context cached. A "patch word" API re-renders just the target word and splices it in, with an automatic seam check (loudness/pace/breath continuity on both sides). Full re-render is the fallback only when the patch fails QC.

techniques.title: Multi-Purpose Data Pipeline Reused as the RL Reward
techniques.what_it_does: The S2 training pipeline uses a speech-quality assessment model and a rich-transcription ASR model to filter and annotate massive audio data for pre-training — then reuses those SAME models as reward signals during RL alignment, explicitly eliminating distribution mismatch between the data stage and the alignment stage.
techniques.why_it_works: If the judge differs from the data filter, the model optimizes toward a different target than the data defined — classic reward hacking surface. Reusing the pipeline as the reward keeps "what counts as good" identical across training stages.
techniques.genesis_implementation: For any voice-module fine-tuning: build one quality-assessment + transcription pipeline, use it to curate training data AND as the reward function. One judge, one standard, everywhere.

techniques.title: Multi-Reward RL Alignment (semantic + acoustic + identity)
techniques.what_it_does: RL alignment jointly optimizes three objectives via a GRPO variant: semantic accuracy (says the right words), acoustic quality (sounds clean), and speaker similarity (sounds like the right person).
techniques.why_it_works: Single-objective RL collapses: optimize only quality and identity drifts; optimize only identity and artifacts creep in. Three explicit rewards keep the trade-off visible and tunable.
techniques.genesis_implementation: Any voice tuning run in the lab module must log all three rewards separately — never a single blended score. If speaker similarity regresses while quality rises, the run is flagged, not shipped. The same triple (accuracy/quality/identity) becomes the QC rubric for every render (W-02).

techniques.title: Rich-Transcription Round-Trip QC
techniques.what_it_does: A rich-transcription model (fine-tuned to transcribe words AND annotate vocal events/turns as natural-language instructions) is used during RL to re-transcribe generated audio and diff it against the original prompt — penalizing hallucinations, missing words, and ignored vocal instructions automatically.
techniques.why_it_works: It turns QC into a closed loop: generation → listen back (machine) → compare → score. Catches the most common TTS failure modes (skipped/repeated words, wrong emotion) without human ears.
techniques.genesis_implementation: Every non-trivial voice render passes through automatic round-trip transcription; word-error and instruction-adherence deltas are logged. workflows.title: TTS Production Pipeline (script → finished audio)
workflows.body:
The pipeline for any non-conversational speech (briefings, announcements,
narrations for the father).

1. **INTAKE** — Text + intent (briefing / announcement) + target voice_id
   + direction note. Entry: voice has a valid P-07 provenance header.
   Exit: intake accepted, or rejected (missing provenance = no render).
2. **NORMALIZE** — P-08 + P-01: strip unpronounceable content, expand
   numbers/acronyms, compute input byte count and cost estimate. Entry:
   intake accepted. Exit: render-ready script + byte cost, or escalation
   if over budget.
3. **DIRECT** — Compile direction (P-02 tags / P-03 director's note) onto
   the normalized script. Entry: render-ready script. Exit: directed
   script with inspectable tag stream.
4. **RENDER** — Generate via the two-stage path (T-01/T-02): semantic plan
   then acoustic render, chunked streaming for long text. Entry: directed
   script. Exit: raw audio.
5. **ROUND-TRIP QC** — Automatic re-transcription (T-11): diff words and
   vocal instructions against the prompt. Check the triple rubric (T-10):
   semantic accuracy, acoustic quality, speaker similarity. Entry: raw
   audio. Exit: PASS → delivery; FAIL → W-02 returns to RENDER (with
   P-06 patch-one-word first), never to delivery.
6. **DELIVER** — Final audio to the requesting module. Entry: QC PASS.
   Exit: delivered with QC report attached (word-error delta, bytes in,
   seconds out, render cost).

Failure modes guarded:
| Failure | Guard |
|---|---|
| Synthetic audio reaches 369 content | Provenance tag checked at delivery; publish gate fails closed on synthetic |
| Mispronunciations / skipped words ship | Round-trip QC fails closed; patch-before-rerender keeps cost down |
| Cost surprise on long renders | Byte count + estimate reported at NORMALIZE, before render |
| Wrong emotion lands on the wrong word | Tag stream is inspectable at DIRECT; QC checks instruction adherence |

techniques.title: Identity-vs-Motion Prompt Separation (the anti-drift rule)
techniques.what_it_does: When character consistency matters, the prompt is split into two labeled blocks. The IDENTITY block carries static visual descriptors ONLY (face features, skin tone, body type, clothing, accessories, palette) — no motion, no camera, no temporal language. The MOTION block carries temporal/camera ONLY (action choreography, camera movement, environmental motion) — no character-appearance repetition.
techniques.why_it_works: Interleaving identity descriptors with motion tokens makes the model re-interpret the face while processing motion, so the face drifts frame to frame. Separation removes the interference; the identity description is applied once, motion applies after.
techniques.genesis_implementation: Encode this as a schema rule in our prompt library: any prompt containing a character reference must have separate `identity` and `motion` fields (validator rejects mixed blocks). This is a generalizable pattern beyond video — apply the same static/dynamic split to any generative asset (avatars, thumbnails, series covers) where a repeated identity must survive variation.

techniques.title: Structured Shot Schema (SCENE / IDENTITY / SHOTS / ANATOMY / PHYSICS / CONTINUITY / LIGHTING / AUDIO / LOOK)

Each section has a defined job; the "bad prompt" failure mode is a shot list of angle names with no assigned job per shot.
techniques.why_it_works: Diffusion video models lose focal points when every sentence is "epic cinematic". Sectioning forces the prompt author to assign each shot a job (establish, product close-up, action payoff), and dedicated anatomy/physics sections suppress the classic hand/deformation artifacts.
techniques.genesis_implementation: Make this schema the mandatory brief format for any GENESIS job that produces a multi-shot video (lab builder scripts, the 369 content team's reel briefs). Provide a brief-template file with the nine sections pre-labeled; the pre-generation gate rejects briefs with an empty CONTINUITY section (that's where "the same product must look the same" lives — the section most prompters skip).

techniques.title: Magic Pills: Control-Word Injection

techniques.why_it_works: It removes prompt-engineering skill as a bottleneck. The structured picker guarantees the words the model responds to are actually present; users can't forget them.
techniques.genesis_implementation: Replicate the mechanic, not the feature: in any GENESIS job that builds prompts (reels, covers, avatar renders), put a "pill picker" layer between the human brief and the final prompt. The picker exposes controlled vocabularies (camera, light, palette, texture); its output is appended verbatim. Log which pills were injected per asset so QC can trace aesthetic decisions.

techniques.title: Genjutsu-Style Motion Preservation (edit the content, keep the motion)
techniques.what_it_does: A video-transformation model takes a source clip (3–30s) plus a change specification (swap character, change background, restyle object) and rebuilds only the specified elements while preserving the original camera motion, VFX, and pacing. Two modes: Motion Transfer (keep motion, change subject) and Object Swap (keep scene, replace element).
techniques.why_it_works: It decouples motion from content. Regenerating a whole clip to fix one bad element wastes budget and risks breaking the parts that were already good; targeted rebuild is cheaper and safer.
techniques.genesis_implementation: Adopt the pattern as a QC repair lane: when a generated video fails review on one element (wrong face, wrong logo), the fix job is scoped to that element with an explicit "preserve" list (motion, timing, composition) rather than a full regeneration. Log the preserve list as part of the fix record — a repair that silently changed the motion is a new failure, not a fix.

techniques.title: Multi-Model Router (one balance, many engines)
techniques.what_it_does: One credit balance spends across 15+ video models and image models; if one model struggles with a particular shot, the same prompt/camera setup reruns through a different engine without leaving the dashboard or buying another subscription. techniques.why_it_works: No single model is best at everything (motion fidelity vs. prompt adherence vs. realism). Routing the shot to the right engine, and retrying a failed shot on a different engine instead of brute-forcing the same one, raises success per credit.
techniques.genesis_implementation: In the scheduler/lab, a generation job records `engine` as a routing decision with a fallback order (primary → fallback engines). A shot that fails QC on the primary engine retries on the next engine with the same camera language (T-01) and identity profile (T-03) before the prompt is rewritten — model mismatch is checked before prompt blame. Cost tier of the engine feeds T-09's estimate.

workflows.title: Character-Consistent Series (episode N of a series)
workflows.body:
For any series with a recurring persona (presenter, character, product line).

1. **PROFILE LOCK** — Identity profile exists (T-03) with multi-angle
   composite sheet (T-14), descriptor block, and palette HEXes; profile
   version recorded.
   Exit: profile ID + version, or STOP (never generate a series without one).
2. **STYLE LOCK** — Style manifest committed (P-07): background/accent HEX,
   lighting preset, texture word. Moodboard for locations/wardrobe (T-13).
   Exit: manifest artifact, versioned.
3. **STORYBOARD** — Shot-job assignments (P-04) for the episode: each shot
   has a job, time window, camera preset, identity reference.
   Exit: storyboard with per-shot jobs; no "whatever angle looks coolest"
   entries.
4. **GENERATE SHOTS** — Per W-01 stages 3–4, shot by shot. End frame of shot
   N becomes start frame of shot N+1 (T-08).
   Exit: all shot artifacts on disk.
5. **CROSS-EPISODE REVIEW** — Compare every shot against the ORIGINAL
   reference set (profile sheet + style manifest), NOT just the previous
   episode (T-08). Continuity non-negotiables (P-08) checked item by item.
   Exit: PASS all shots, or repair list scoped per shot (W-03).
6. **ASSEMBLE** — Stitch, grade to manifest, audio mix (P-09), export.
   Exit: finished episode + full provenance (profile version, manifest
   version, engine log).

**Guarded failure modes:**
- Face/outfit drift detected at step 5 → repair lane on the drifted shots
  only; if a repair alters identity, the profile is RE-versioned and the
  change is logged (identity never changes silently).
- A shot's hero frame fails lock → that shot does not enter generation;
  the pipeline continues with other shots (no blocked shots held as
  half-done).

workflows.title: QC Repair Loop (generate → verify → targeted fix)
workflows.body:
The standard correction workflow; full regeneration is the last resort.

1. **TRIAGE** — Classify each QC failure: element-changeable (face, logo,
   background) vs. motion-fundamental (wrong camera move, wrong pacing).
   Exit: classified failure list.
2. **SCOPE REPAIR** — For element failures: write the repair prompt with an
   explicit preserve list (motion, timing, composition, audio) (P-10,
   T-07).
   Exit: repair spec; anything not on the change list is frozen.
3. **REPAIR** — Execute the scoped repair (max 2 rounds).
   Exit: repaired artifact, or escalation.
4. **RE-VERIFY** — QC the repaired clip against the brief AND confirm the
   preserve list actually held (a repair that changed the motion is a new
   failure).
   Exit: PASS, or escalate.
5. **RECORD** — Store failure → repair → verified outcome as a confirmed
   memory record (only verified repairs enter memory).

**Guarded failure modes:**
- Repair changes a preserved element → the repair job is marked FAILED
  (not the original clip); original artifact is retained.
- Motion-fundamental failures skip this loop → they go to regeneration or
  engine fallback (W-04); never try to "repair" a wrong camera move.

workflows.title: Multi-Engine Fallback (shot routing)
workflows.body:
For shots that fail on the primary engine.

1. **DIAGNOSE** — Determine whether the failure is engine-mismatch
   (engine's known weakness, e.g. weak motion coherence) or prompt-mismatch.
   Exit: classified; only engine-mismatch proceeds here.
2. **ROUTE** — Select the next engine in the fallback order whose strength
   matches the shot's need (motion-heavy → motion-strong engine; realism →
   realism engine), keeping camera preset (P-03) and identity profile
   (P-01) identical.
   Exit: fallback engine selected, same control spec.
3. **REGENERATE** — Rerun with the identical prompt/controls on the new
   engine. Cost re-estimated and re-authorized (T-09).
   Exit: new artifact, or next fallback.
4. **COMPARE** — Side-by-side QC of the best artifacts from each engine.
   Exit: winner selected with reasons recorded (engine lesson stored as
   confirmed memory: "shot type X → engine Y").

- Fallback list exhausted (all engines tried) → escalate to human director
  with the comparison grid; do not loop back to engine 1 automatically.
- A fallback engine costs more than the authorized budget → STOP and ask;
  the router never upgrades spend on its own.

techniques.title: Frames-to-Video: Start/End Frame Lock (in-betweening)
techniques.what_it_does: The user supplies a start frame, an end frame, or both; the model generates the animated transition between them — interpolating motion, lighting changes, and scene evolution.
techniques.why_it_works: It replaces the weakest part of generative video (the model inventing the whole composition) with the strongest part (motion interpolation). The creator controls exactly how the shot begins and ends; the model only fills the middle.
techniques.genesis_implementation: When deterministic framing matters, prefer the frame-lock path: render stills first (Imagen or a frame-extraction step), lock them as start/end, then animate. Do not start from a text-only prompt when a composed frame is affordable — the still is cheaper to QC than a failed 8-second render. For 369 reels: generate the hero cover frame first (reviewed, approved), then animate it into the opening shot — never let the opening frame be a surprise.

techniques.why_it_works: Prompt-time direction bakes camera into the generation; post-generation adjustment decouples the camera decision from the subject decision, letting a creator fix composition without re-rolling the whole shot.
techniques.genesis_implementation: Separate camera specification into a structured `camera` object (preset name + intensity), never prose buried in the prompt body. Keep a `CAMERA_PRESETS` registry (dolly, crane, orbit, tracking, handheld, crash zoom, whip pan, Dutch tilt, static...). For generated video work: always attempt prompt-time direction first; treat post-generation camera adjustment as the cheap fix before re-generation.

techniques.title: Flow TV: Exact-Prompt Public Gallery as a Learning Loop
techniques.what_it_does: A built-in showcase of clips where viewers can see the exact prompts and techniques used for each piece — creators learn by copying real working prompts, not by reading tutorials.
techniques.why_it_works: Prompt knowledge is tacit; the fastest transfer is artifact + recipe together. The gallery converts every good generation into a teaching example for the whole user base.
techniques.genesis_implementation: Keep a permanent `prompt_library` in memory where every approved asset stores its full prompt, model, settings, and result thumbnail. prompt_patterns.title: Five-Layer Prompt Formula (Flow's official grammar)
prompt_patterns.use_when: writing any video-generation prompt.
prompt_patterns.pattern: Build the prompt as five explicit layers, in order. Missing layers get filled by the model with something average — fill them yourself.
prompt_patterns.template: > [Cinematography] + [Subject] + [Action] + [Context] + [Style & Ambiance] > Cinematography: <shot type, angle, movement, lens effect> > Subject: <who/what, specific visual traits, role> > Action: <ONE primary action, interactions, expression> > Context: <environment, era, objects, light sources> > Style & Ambiance: <color grade, mood, texture, reference name>
prompt_patterns.raw:
- **Use when:** writing any video-generation prompt.
- **Pattern:** Build the prompt as five explicit layers, in order. Missing
  layers get filled by the model with something average — fill them yourself.
- **Template:**
  > [Cinematography] + [Subject] + [Action] + [Context] + [Style & Ambiance]
  > Cinematography: <shot type, angle, movement, lens effect>
  > Subject: <who/what, specific visual traits, role>
  > Action: <ONE primary action, interactions, expression>
  > Context: <environment, era, objects, light sources>
  > Style & Ambiance: <color grade, mood, texture, reference name>

prompt_patterns.title: Reference-Lock Block (ingredients header)
prompt_patterns.use_when: a recurring character, object, or style appears in the shot.
prompt_patterns.pattern: Name the locked assets up front; never re-describe them in prose.
prompt_patterns.template: > INGREDIENTS: [subject_ref_v2] [style_moodboard_urban-night] > SUBJECT: the reference subject, same face, same jacket > The rest of the prompt carries only what CHANGES in this shot.

  > The rest of the prompt carries only what CHANGES in this shot.

prompt_patterns.title: Frame-Lock Sandwich (start/end anchors)
prompt_patterns.use_when: you know exactly how the shot should begin and end.
prompt_patterns.pattern: Lock the frames; let the model fill only the middle.
prompt_patterns.template: > START FRAME: [still_asset_01] > END FRAME: [still_asset_02] > TRANSITION: <what happens between — motion, lighting shift, camera> > Rule: compose and approve both stills before spending any video budget.

prompt_patterns.title: Coverage Grammar (shot vocabulary per scene)
prompt_patterns.use_when: planning a scene of more than one shot.
prompt_patterns.pattern: Every scene gets coverage from the same fixed vocabulary so the sequence cuts together: establishing / medium / close-up, with named camera moves.
prompt_patterns.template: > SCENE: <beat description> > COVERAGE: 1. Establishing: <environment, wide> 2. Medium: <subject in > context> 3. Close-up: <detail, emotion, object> 4. (optional) Insert. > Camera per shot: <preset name from the CAMERA_PRESETS registry>. > 369 rule: each coverage note carries its text timing (text ≥ 3s on screen).

prompt_patterns.use_when: the shot needs a specific camera move.
prompt_patterns.pattern: Choose the camera as a named preset token in the Cinematography layer; decide deliberately whether it is baked at prompt time or fixed in post.

Named references produce a human-directed look.)

prompt_patterns.title: Variation-Set Pattern (one asset × N looks)
prompt_patterns.use_when: comparing visual directions before committing.
prompt_patterns.pattern: Generate the SAME composition under N lighting/mood variants; pick one as the lock; archive the rest.
prompt_patterns.template: > BASE: [composed still, approved] > VARIANTS: <N=5–8: lighting/mood/grrade each stated as a named look> > DECISION: winner → INGREDIENT for the scene. Losers → archived, never > deleted (they train future taste). --- ## Composition rule A single shot is **P-01 (five layers) + P-03 (reference lock) + P-07 (camera token)**. Add **P-05 (audio)** when sound matters, **P-04 (frame lock)** when composition is pre-decided. A scene is **P-06 (coverage)** sequenced in SceneBuilder; longer than ~32s uses **P-08 (extend chain)** with QC checkpoints. A distinctive look is **P-10 (variation set) → winner → P-09 (style lock)**; locked looks go into the ingredient library and the team's prompt library (T-06: Flow TV pattern). A revision is a **masked/conversational fix on the artifact** (T-09, T-12) — re-roll the full shot only with a recorded reason. ## Sources Distilled from Google's public Veo prompting guidance and independent community guides (skill documents, review sites, filmmaker workflow coverage). All wording is our own.

  > VARIANTS: <N=5–8: lighting/mood/grrade each stated as a named look>
  > DECISION: winner → INGREDIENT for the scene. Losers → archived, never
  > deleted (they train future taste).

## Composition rule

A single shot is **P-01 (five layers) + P-03 (reference lock) + P-07
(camera token)**. Add **P-05 (audio)** when sound matters, **P-04
(frame lock)** when composition is pre-decided.

A scene is **P-06 (coverage)** sequenced in SceneBuilder; longer than
~32s uses **P-08 (extend chain)** with QC checkpoints.

A distinctive look is **P-10 (variation set) → winner → P-09 (style
lock)**; locked looks go into the ingredient library and the team's
prompt library (T-06: Flow TV pattern).

A revision is a **masked/conversational fix on the artifact** (T-09,
T-12) — re-roll the full shot only with a recorded reason.

workflows.title: Idea → Film Pipeline (the master sequence)
workflows.body:
The master workflow. Every video deliverable follows it.

1. **INTAKE** — Receive the brief: goal (what the film must do), constraints
   (budget, tier, models allowed), done-means (how QC judges it).
   Exit: concrete, verifiable goal; otherwise one clarifying question.
2. **PLAN AS SHOTS** — Break the idea into a shot list (P-06 coverage:
   establishing/medium/close-up). Each shot gets: the five-layer prompt
   (P-01), ingredients (P-03), camera token (P-07), audio spec (P-05).
   Exit: written shot list with per-shot locks; no locks, no render.
3. **LOCK THE LOOK** — Moodboard → variation set (P-10) → winning style
   ingredient (P-09). Exit: one locked moodboard attached to every shot.
4. **DRAFT CHEAP** — Render each shot at the lowest tier (T-07): composition
   and timing only. Exit: drafts approved for composition; identity defects
   are expected and ignored at this tier.
5. **RENDER HEROES** — Standard/hero tier only for shots whose drafts passed.
   Frame-lock (P-04) where composition is pre-decided. Exit: all hero clips
   rendered; failed ones fixed by masked edit (T-09) or re-rendered with a
   recorded reason.
6. **ASSEMBLE** — SceneBuilder-style timeline (T-04): arrange, trim, order;
   extend-chains (P-08) for sequences over ~32s with QC checkpoints.
   Exit: timed assembly; every on-screen text ≥3s (the reel law).
7. **AUDIO PASS** — Verify native audio per clip; repair the audio lane for
   extended/masked chains (T-05) — re-record or layer SFX as needed.
   Exit: full mix, no silent gaps, no desync.
8. **MERCILESS REVIEW** — Independent scored review (LAW-050), including the
   anti-AI-slop criterion (LAW-149): nothing generic, glossy, or formulaic
   passes. Exit: PASS or fix-list.
9. **DELIVER** — Export (MP4/WebM/frames), archive prompts + ingredients +
   settings into the prompt library (T-06 Flow TV pattern), spend report.
   Exit: father sees only the finished outcome.

Failure mode guarded: skipping locks (step 2–3) and going straight to render —
blocked by the pre-generation validator.

workflows.title: Style-Lock Workflow (moodboard → locked look)
workflows.body:
For establishing a repeatable visual identity before any production (T-08,
P-09/P-10; the 369 page-DNA process formalized).

1. **COLLECT** — 3–6 references: own past work, licensed/official sources,
   never copyrighted material. Exit: reference set with sources noted.
2. **COLLAG**E — Assemble the moodboard: palette, texture, lens character,
   grade direction. Exit: one board the whole team can see.
3. **VARIANTS** — Render the same base composition under 5–8 named looks.
   Exit: side-by-side set.
4. **CHOOSE** — Human (or Agent YZ) picks one winner; the choice and its
   reason are recorded. Exit: one locked look with a name and a version.
5. **INGREDIENT-IZE** — The locked look becomes a style ingredient attached
   to every shot of the project. Exit: no shot renders without it.

Entry: a project needing a distinctive look. Exit: locked style
ingredient, versioned. Failure mode guarded: adjective-style ("cinematic")
— blocked at step 2; the board must be visual, never verbal. Directly
serves LAW-149: a locked human-directed look is the opposite of AI slop.

workflows.title: Agentic Batch Production (Flow Agent pattern, for scheduler)
workflows.body:
For producing many assets or variants unattended (T-14, Astra W-01/W-05).

1. **CHARTER** — Standing goal + boundaries + budget tier + approval classes
   (P-06 of Astra). Stored, versioned, reviewable.
2. **PLAN-AS-PACK** — The agent emits a storyboard/prompt pack: shot list,
   prompts, ingredients, tiers. Reviewable BEFORE any spend.
   Exit: pack approved (human or policy gate).
3. **QUEUED EXECUTION** — Renders run in the background per the pack; the
   agent watches, auto-recovers cheap failures, escalates per gate class.
   Exit: all pack items rendered or blocked with evidence.
4. **HOUSEKEEPING** — Files renamed by convention, media sorted into named
   collections, unused assets archived (T-13).
   Exit: collection tidy, register complete.
5. **PROACTIVE REPORT** — Milestones and surprises reported out; the father
   sees finished outcomes, not render logs.
   Exit: delivery + spend report + prompt-library updates.

Entry: approved charter. Exit: finished assets + tidy collection + report.
Failure mode guarded: silent spend and anonymous assets — blocked by the
pack-approval gate and the naming/collection rules.

techniques.why_it_works: Prompt-engineering the same face description every time drifts — each generation is a new roll of the dice. A trained identity token converts identity from a hope into an input, making consistency a property of the system rather than luck.
techniques.genesis_implementation: [FEEDS-369-LIBRARY] Build an identity-registry pattern in the lab module: a reference asset (photo set or approved key art) is embedded once; every subsequent generation carries that embedding as a conditioning input. techniques.what_it_does: One generation credit returns four candidate images in ~20 seconds; the user picks the best instead of re-rolling blindly.
techniques.why_it_works: Selection beats iteration. Four parallel candidates cost roughly the same compute as one, but give the human a real choice and cut the "regenerate until acceptable" loop that burns credits and time.

techniques.title: Director-Mode Framing (explicit composition metadata)
techniques.what_it_does: Director Mode lets the user position and scale the character inside a defined aspect ratio (1:1, 3:2, 2:3) — framing is a control surface, not something begged from the prompt.
techniques.why_it_works: Prompts are unreliable for spatial layout ("put him on the left" often fails). Explicit framing metadata (canvas ratio + subject zone + scale) is deterministic where language is fuzzy.
techniques.genesis_implementation: [FEEDS-369-LIBRARY] Every generation brief carries a `canvas` spec: aspect ratio, subject zone (rule-of-thirds cell), and scale band. The lab module enforces it at composition time (crop/pad/reframe step) rather than hoping the model obeys. This also kills the classic safe-area failure — text/logos get protected zones by construction.

prompt_patterns.title: Expression-Action Clause
prompt_patterns.use_when: the face must carry a specific emotion or action.
prompt_patterns.pattern: One emotion + one physical verb, placed right after the identity anchor. Public walkthroughs show expressions are the least reliable part — so keep the clause SHORT and verifiable (you can see it or you can't).
prompt_patterns.template: > <identity>, <emotion: shocked / determined / amused>, <verb: raising one > eyebrow / mouth slightly open / leaning forward>. > QC: if the expression is not visible in the output, regenerate — never > "interpret" a wrong expression as acceptable.

prompt_patterns.title: Environment-First Scene Anchoring
prompt_patterns.use_when: placing a fixed identity into varied worlds (the "reimagine yourself anywhere" pattern).
prompt_patterns.pattern: Describe the ENVIRONMENT completely, then drop the identity into it with a placement verb. The environment is the variable; the identity is the constant.
prompt_patterns.template: > Environment: <location, time of day, lighting, atmosphere>. > <identity> standing in the <placement: center-left / foreground>, > <interaction with environment: holding a lantern / rain on shoulders>. > Cinematic depth, background softly detailed, subject in sharp focus.

prompt_patterns.title: Dual-Subject Composition Brief
prompt_patterns.use_when: two locked identities must share one frame.

prompt_patterns.use_when: commissioning a generation run where you will pick a winner.

prompt_patterns.title: Anti-Slop Specificity Stack
prompt_patterns.use_when: the output must pass LAW-149 (never look like generic AI slop).
prompt_patterns.pattern: Stack CONCRETE material and light details — real things have texture, weight, and imperfection. Generic outputs come from generic words.
prompt_patterns.template: > Replace every vague adjective with a material fact: > not "beautiful jacket" → "worn brown leather jacket, creased at the > elbows, brass zipper"; > not "nice lighting" → "late-afternoon sun through blinds, dust in the air"; > not "detailed face" → "faint scar above the left eyebrow, stubble > shadow at the jaw". > Negative: airbrushed skin, plastic shine, symmetrical perfection, > stock-photo smile.

## Composition rule

A full portrait-generation brief is P-01 (identity) + P-04 (scene) + P-02
(style + negative tail) + P-06 (batch selection criteria). Add P-03 when a
specific expression is required, P-05 when two subjects share the frame, P-08
when a template owns the layout. P-07 (anti-slop specificity) is MANDATORY on
every brief that could reach the 369 technique library — a brief without
material specificity is rejected at the gate. P-09 governs how non-English
briefs enter the pipeline. P-10 stays in the lab for architecture study; it
never reaches 369 production.

workflows.title: Identity Onboarding (train once, reuse forever)
workflows.body:
- **Entry criteria:** 10–20 clear face photos (single subject, varied angles,
  good light); written consent for likeness use on file; target use declared
  (portrait series / video / template fills).
- **Steps:**
  1. Validate photo set (face detectable in all, no second person, mouth
     visible in ≥3).
  2. Train identity token (10–30 min class of job; tracked as a scheduled job
     with progress events).
  3. Verification pass: generate 4 test portraits across 2 styles; likeness
     score vs reference embedding ≥ threshold on all 4.
  4. Register identity: store token id, reference embedding, consent record,
     version number.
- **Exit criteria:** identity token registered with 4/4 likeness tests passing;
  consent record attached; cost logged.
- **Guarded failure modes:**
  - Photo set fails validation → return the failing photos with reasons;
    NEVER train on a weak set (a weak identity poisons everything downstream).
  - Likeness test < threshold → retrain with augmented set (more angles) or
    reject identity; never ship a "close enough" token.
  - Consent missing → job blocked at the gate; no override path.

workflows.title: Consistent Series Production (batch → select → finish)
workflows.body:
- **Entry criteria:** registered identity (W-01) or locked reference set;
  brief composed per the composition rule (P-01+P-04+P-02+P-06, P-07 mandatory);
  continuity manifest for the series (palette, style_id, footer, canvas).
- **Steps:**
  1. Generate batch of 4 variants (1 credit-class cost).
  2. Score each: likeness vs identity embedding, composition vs canvas spec,
     anti-slop checklist (LAW-149 criteria).
  3. Human/agent selects winner (top likeness score is the default, not the
     mandate — selection is a decision, logged).
  4. Finishing chain on the winner only: clean (background/safe-area) →
     upscale → final QC.
  5. Continuity check vs series manifest; append to series registry.
- **Exit criteria:** winner selected with logged reason; finishing chain
  complete; continuity check passing; credit cost reconciled.
- **Guarded failure modes:**
  - All 4 variants fail likeness → diagnose (prompt drift? weak identity?)
    and regenerate ONCE with tightened brief; second total failure escalates
    to identity re-verification (W-01 step 3), never to endless re-rolls.
  - Winner fails continuity vs manifest → rejected; series does not accept an
    off-family piece to "save the credit."
  - Finishing chain skipped → piece cannot enter the publish queue; the chain
    is a gate, not a suggestion.

workflows.title: Template-Driven Campaign (theme packs at volume)
workflows.body:
- **Entry criteria:** campaign brief (theme, count, platforms); template set
  approved by the format authority; identity tokens registered (or "no
  identity" declared for non-character pieces).
- **Steps:**
  1. Instantiate templates: each slot filled by P-08 (identity + ≤10-word
     scene keywords; text zones reserved, never AI-generated text).
  2. Batch generate (variant batches per slot, W-02 selection per slot).
  3. Series continuity pass: all pieces checked against the campaign manifest
     as a SET, not individually — the family must read as one.
  4. Bulk export at per-platform specs; registry updated with piece ids,
     templates, costs.
- **Exit criteria:** full set delivered at spec; set-level continuity passing;
  per-piece costs reconciled to campaign budget.
- **Guarded failure modes:**
  - One slot keeps failing → swap the template for that slot (templates are
    interchangeable by design) rather than burning credits on a bad fit.
  - Set-level continuity fails → identify the outlier piece(s); regenerate
    the outliers against the manifest, never "accept the set anyway."
  - AI-generated text appears in an image → piece rejected; text is rendered
    by the type system downstream, never by the generator (PERSIAN/typography
    laws apply to all on-piece text).

techniques.title: Natively Multimodal Generation Architecture
techniques.what_it_does: The generator is built on the same multimodal transformer lineage as the language models: it accepts text AND image inputs together and produces image outputs in one system. Editing, reference-based generation, and text-to-image all flow through the same model instead of a pipeline of separate tools.
techniques.why_it_works: Splitting generation into separate tools (one for text, one for image, a blender in between) creates mismatch errors. A single model that sees both modalities can bind prompt words directly to image regions, which is why instruction following and edit precision jumped when the architecture changed.
techniques.genesis_implementation: If we ever build local image capability, treat it as one module that takes (text, images) jointly, not a text→image bolt-on. Short term: this technique informs how we CALL external models — always pass the full brief (text) plus all references (images) in ONE request instead of chaining separate generation and compositing steps.

techniques.title: Masked Inpainting With Alpha Masks
techniques.what_it_does: A mask image defines edit regions: alpha-channel transparency carries the selection (transparent pixels are regenerated, opaque pixels are preserved). This gives surgical control — change one object or region without touching the rest of the frame.
techniques.why_it_works: Global prompt edits always risk collateral changes. A spatial mask decouples WHERE from WHAT: the mask says where, the prompt says what. Precision work (fix one hand, change one label) becomes reliable.
techniques.genesis_implementation: Build mask generation as a first-class operation: bounding-box/segmentation → alpha mask → inpainting call. Always pair an inpaint call with a generated mask rather than asking the model to "figure out which part" from text alone. Log mask + prompt + before/after for every surgical edit.

techniques.title: Structured Five-Section Prompt Template
techniques.what_it_does: Practitioners converged on a sectioned brief template: Scene (where/when/environment), Subject (main focus, with the identity anchor repeated identically), Important details (composition, lighting, style references, materials, mood), Use case (the deliverable format and layout), Constraints (preserve/keep instructions, hard rules). Effective prompts land around 250–400 words; longer ones give diminishing returns.
techniques.why_it_works: Sections force the brief-writer to answer every question the model needs (scene, subject, craft, format, limits) and keep them from bleeding into each other. The length ceiling reflects the model's real attention budget: past ~400 words, added detail gets ignored or contradicts earlier detail.
techniques.genesis_implementation: Make this template a code artifact, not a document: a prompt-builder function with the five slots, a word-count check that warns past 400, and automatic verbatim injection of identity anchors into the Subject slot (see T-03). Every asset brief flows through the builder; no raw free-text prompts in production.

techniques.title: Transparent Background Compositing
techniques.what_it_does: Generation calls can request transparent backgrounds (PNG/WebP), producing isolated subjects ready for layering into layouts, thumbnails, and motion graphics without chroma-key hacks.
techniques.why_it_works: It separates subject creation from composition. The subject can be shot once and reused across layouts, sizes, and formats — the exact workflow our carousel/thumbnail teams already do by hand.
techniques.genesis_implementation: Prefer native transparency over post-hoc background removal in every asset pipeline: request it at generation time with a transparent-capable format. Keep a library of isolated subjects (products, props, graphic elements) as reusable layers, versioned like code, composited by the layout module.

techniques.title: Provenance Marking (C2PA metadata)
techniques.what_it_does: Generated images carry C2PA content-credential metadata marking them as AI-generated, alongside the vendor's safety guardrails (content filtering with a moderation sensitivity control).
techniques.why_it_works: Provenance survives where labels don't: metadata travels with the file. For a network that must track what is AI-made vs. real footage (our breaking-news and review requirements), embedded provenance is the only honest bookkeeping.
techniques.genesis_implementation: Adopt the same discipline internally: every AI-generated asset in our world gets metadata stamped (tool, model, date, job id, seed) at creation time. Human/real art gets a different stamp. Our review gates can then enforce rules by provenance (e.g. "no AI faces in this slot") instead of by guesswork. Note the compliance tension with our NO AI DISCLOSURE law: internal provenance (metadata) is mandatory; visible disclosure in 369 output is governed by the law, which stands per YZ's ruling.

techniques.title: Positive Framing Over Negative Prompts
techniques.what_it_does: Practitioners found negative prompts ("NOT a painting, NOT glowing") can backfire: the model often latches onto the negated keyword and renders it anyway. The working fix is positive specification — describe what should be there ("eyes left as raw unpainted canvas") instead of what should not.
techniques.why_it_works: These models are trained to complete imagery from descriptions; negation is a weak signal against the pull of the mentioned concept. Positive description gives the model something concrete to render, which crowds out the unwanted default.
techniques.genesis_implementation: Our prompt builder should include a lint rule: flag "no / not / without / don't" constructions and require a positive restatement before the call goes out. - **What it does:** Practitioners found negative prompts ("NOT a painting,
  NOT glowing") can backfire: the model often latches onto the negated
  keyword and renders it anyway. The working fix is positive specification —
  describe what should be there ("eyes left as raw unpainted canvas")
  instead of what should not.
- **Why it works:** These models are trained to complete imagery from
  descriptions; negation is a weak signal against the pull of the mentioned
  concept. Positive description gives the model something concrete to render,
  which crowds out the unwanted default.
- **GENESIS implementation:** Our prompt builder should include a lint rule:
  flag "no / not / without / don't" constructions and require a positive
  restatement before the call goes out. Negative constraints stay in the
  Constraints slot only as explicit hard rules (which behave differently),
  never as the main descriptive language.

## Capability signals: vendor claims vs. independent evidence

| Capability | Vendor claim | Independent evidence | GENESIS read |
|---|---|---|---|
| Precise instruction-following in edits | Stronger instruction following; changes only requested elements | Community reports of instruction drift, substituted elements, ignored constraints (Oct 2026) | Treat as unreliable: verify every edit against the brief; budget for regeneration |
| Text rendering (dense/small text) | Improved accuracy, fewer spelling errors, dense text support | Generally confirmed as a real leap; still collapses on dense technical layouts | Usable for drafts/mockups; sealed 369 text = code-composited, not model-rendered |
| Speed | Up to 4x faster than predecessor | Roughly confirmed (seconds vs. a minute+), peak lag persists | Design workflows around seconds-scale latency; batch queue accordingly |
| Multi-turn edit consistency | Maintains earlier changes across rounds | Mixed: many users report "fix one thing, break another" cycles | Implement T-02 with per-round acceptance checks; never trust continuity blindly |
| Face/identity preservation | Preserves lighting, composition, appearance across edits | Anatomy still unreliable (hands, limbs, interactions); repeated re-generation causes identity drift (model-collapse observations) | High-fidelity edits + identity anchors (T-03/T-06) + human QC on faces |
| Style/brand consistency | Close adherence to style references | "Close, not exact" — brand identity matching is hit-or-miss; grid/layout precision (grids, concentric circles) unreliable | Style anchors reduce but don't solve; brand-critical geometry = code |
| Multi-face scenes | Improved generation with multiple faces | Improved but not reliable; complex poses/interactions still error-prone | Avoid multi-figure hero shots for 369 unless QC passes |
| Safety filtering | Guardrails with moderation sensitivity control | Widely reported as over-broad and inconsistent (legitimate adult/non-explicit art blocked) | Expect false rejections; design retry/redirect paths; never promise what the filter may refuse |

## Real-world use cases (public evidence)

Strong fits: product images and e-commerce hero shots, product background
variations, ad creative concepts, social graphics and thumbnails, editorial
illustrations, campaign image sets, infographics and layout drafts, source
frames for video work. Caution zones (practitioners flag these): final legal
brand identities, exact product labels without review, official-looking
documents, copyrighted-character imitation, final commercial-print typography,
anything requiring guaranteed factual accuracy.

- Anatomy unreliable: extra/missing limbs, distorted hands, wrong joints,
  implausible character interactions — explicit correct-anatomy prompts do
  not reliably prevent this.
- Instruction drift: the assistant can restate instructions correctly in

workflows.title: Concept → Final Asset (explore → anchor → refine → QC → deliver)
workflows.body:
The master production workflow for a single hero image.

1. **BRIEF** — Write the P-01 sectioned brief (Scene/Subject/Details/Use
   case/Constraints), 250–400 words. Entry: the deliverable spec is known
   (size, format, where it ships). Exit: brief passes the lint (positive
   framing per P-05, hero front-loaded per P-02, no vague words).
2. **EXPLORE** — Generate 2–4 variants at LOW quality (T-08 draft tier).
   Exit: one direction chosen by the reviewer; the rest are discarded, not
   stored.
3. **ANCHOR** — Lock the winning direction: generate or select the reference
   assets (T-04 role-labeled references) and write the P-03 consistency
   block if anything must recur. Exit: reference set + consistency block
   are versioned and stored with the job.
4. **RENDER** — One generation at MEDIUM or HIGH quality with the full
   brief, references, and size/format locked (T-11 transparent PNG if the
   asset is a layer). Exit: a render that matches the brief on structure,
   subject, and style.
5. **QC** — Independent review against the brief: spelling of every quoted
   string (P-04), anatomy sanity, no collateral changes, brand-fit check.
   Exit: PASS, or a single specific fix-list for one edit round.
6. **DELIVER** — Final file + job record (prompt, seed, references, cost,
   provenance stamp per T-12). Exit: the asset is in its library with a
   name and version; the reviewer, not the generator, signed off.

Failure modes guarded: prompt bloat (word-count lint in BRIEF),
draft-priced finals (quality ladder enforced by stage), unverified "done"
claims (QC before DELIVER), anonymous assets (job record with provenance).

techniques.title: Adaptive Effort Thinking (reasoning depth matched to difficulty)
techniques.what_it_does: The model decides per request how much to think, governed by an effort setting (low / medium / high / max) instead of a fixed token budget. Simple queries skip thinking entirely; hard ones reason deeply. In the coding harness, depth can also be escalated with thinking keywords ("think" → "think harder" → "ultrathink").
techniques.why_it_works: Fixed budgets starve hard tasks and waste tokens on easy ones. Adaptive thinking couples compute spend to actual difficulty, and the visible thinking trace becomes inspectable debugging material when something goes wrong.
techniques.genesis_implementation: Add `effort` to the scheduler's job schema and to the lab/hands reasoning policy (low = act directly, high = deliberate first). Log thinking tokens per job. Default to medium; escalate on verify-failure only. Thinking spend is surfaced in the pre-execution report, honoring the father's zero-spend discipline.

workflows.title: Agentic Coding Loop (explore → plan → approve → execute → verify → commit)
workflows.body:
The master coding workflow. Every GENESIS code job follows it.

1. **EXPLORE** — Fan out parallel specialist subagents (T-03) with bounded
   specs (P-01): codebase patterns, related modules, dependencies. JIT
   retrieval (P-05, T-07): identifiers in, content on demand.
   Exit: merged findings summary; orchestrator understands the terrain.
2. **PLAN** — Strong-model planner writes the plan: files to touch, change per
   file, verify method per change (T-04).
   Exit: written plan with per-step verification.
3. **APPROVE** — Plan gate (P-02, T-10). Execution is blocked until the plan
   carries an approval record (T-06 deterministic hook enforces this).
   Exit: approved plan, or revise-and-resubmit.
4. **EXECUTE** — Interleaved think–act–verify per step (T-02): reflect after
   every tool result; visible task list updated (P-09); effort calibrated
   per step (T-01).
   Exit: all steps verified, or blocked with evidence.
5. **VERIFY** — Run acceptance checks; completion claims require proof
   artifacts (P-08).
   Exit: PASS with evidence, or fix-list back to EXECUTE.
6. **COMMIT** — Descriptive commit per verified increment (T-11); update the
   feature checklist (T-09); store confirmed learnings only.
   Exit: clean mergeable state + checklist updated.

workflows.title: Parallel Research Synthesis (orchestrator + researcher fan-out)
workflows.body:
For questions no single context window can answer alone.

1. **SCOPE** — Orchestrator writes the exact questions; assigns one bounded
   brief per researcher (P-01).
   Exit: question list + researcher specs, no overlap between briefs.
2. **FAN-OUT** — Researchers run in parallel with narrowed tools; each returns
   a condensed summary (≤2,000 tokens), never raw dumps (T-03).
   Exit: one summary per researcher.
3. **CROSS-CHECK** — Orchestrator marks facts appearing in only one source as
   unverified; vendor claims stay vendor-reported until independently
   confirmed.
   Exit: findings table with confidence + sources per fact.
4. **SYNTHESIZE** — Answer each question: finding, confidence, sources, what
   remains unknown.
   Exit: synthesis document with the Persian summary header.
5. **FILE** — Write to the knowledge store; confirmed learnings only.

workflows.title: Clean-Window Review Loop (independent second eye)
workflows.body:
For anything that ships: code, documents, plans. Complements — not replaces —
our Kiro/9Router external second-eye route.

1. **FREEZE** — The change set is frozen; author stops touching it.
   Exit: immutable change artifact + acceptance criteria.
2. **ISOLATE** — A reviewer subagent is spawned with a fresh context: the
   change + the criteria only. No author notes, no reasoning trace (P-10).
   Read-only tools.
   Exit: reviewer briefed, author's window untouched.
3. **ATTACK** — Reviewer produces a severity-ordered flaw report
   (BLOCKER / MAJOR / MINOR) with exact locations; praise is not a finding.
   Exit: report delivered, or explicit PASS with the checklist it verified.
4. **ADJUDICATE** — Orchestrator triages: BLOCKERs return the change to the
   author; MINORs are logged as follow-ups.
   Exit: fix-list or PASS.
5. **CLOSE** — PASS record stored with what was checked; the reviewer's report
   is filed as the review evidence.

How it complements Kiro/9Router: Kiro/9Router is an *external* second opinion
(a different model, an independent session) — strong against our blind spots
but outside the workflow. W-03 is an *internal* independent check — the change
judged against its own approved plan and acceptance criteria, inside the
workflow, before anything leaves it. External catches what we can't see;
internal catches what doesn't match what we promised. Two gates, different
failure classes, both required before ship.

techniques.title: Log-Driven Autonomous Debugging (first ERROR wins)
techniques.what_it_does: When a build breaks, the agent reads the deployment/runtime logs and finds the FIRST line marked ERROR or FAILED — that is usually the root cause. It then fixes that one fault and re-runs, instead of reacting to the last symptom in the chain.
techniques.why_it_works: Error chains cascade: the last error is almost always a downstream symptom. Starting at the first failure short-circuits the symptom-chasing loop that burns the most credits and patience.
techniques.genesis_implementation: In the hands error handler, classify failures by scanning logs chronologically and pinning the first fatal line as the diagnosis anchor. Only after fixing the anchor may the agent re-run; fixing later lines first is classified as a policy violation. Log the anchor line in the job's failure record so the same anchor is never re-investigated twice (feeds the memory module's failure→solution store).

workflows.title: Debug→Fix Loop (for lab / hands coding work)
workflows.body:
For: anything broken in a build, preview, or live deployment.

1. **REPRODUCE** — State the symptom and reproduce it in the preview.
   Exit: the failure is observable and repeatable.
   Failure guard: if it cannot be reproduced, stop — do not "fix" what you
   cannot see.
2. **ANCHOR** — Read the logs chronologically; pin the FIRST ERROR/FAILED
   line as the diagnosis anchor (T-07, P-05).
   Exit: one anchor line identified.
   Failure guard: fixing a later symptom line first is a policy violation;
   the run is reset to this step.
3. **ISOLATE** — Check the memory module for a confirmed fix for this anchor
   before writing new code (recall-before-action).
   Exit: either a known fix is applied, or the fault is genuinely novel.
4. **FIX** — Smallest possible change addressing the anchor. One change, one
   re-run.
   Exit: anchor error gone and previous passing criteria still pass.
   Failure guard: after 3 failed fix attempts on the same anchor, escalate
   to the human with the anchor line + attempted fixes. Never enter an
   unbounded fix loop (T-08, T-14 budget).
5. **REGRESS** — Re-run the self-test suite (W-01 step 4) to confirm nothing
   else broke.
   Exit: full suite green. The confirmed fix (anchor → fix → green run) is

techniques.raw:
- **What it does:** Third-party apps plug into the chat surface (Gmail, Drive,
  GitHub, Notion, Slack…): the assistant can pull from them and act through
  them with existing app permissions, including inside voice conversations.
  Permissions are per-app and restrictions carry over across surfaces.
- **Why it works:** The assistant becomes useful where the user's data lives
  instead of where the chat lives. Permission continuity (same restrictions
  in voice, text, and Work) keeps one security model instead of three.
- **GENESIS implementation:** For hands + lab: an app-connector registry with
  one permission model applied identically to every surface (chat, voice,
  scheduled runs). Connectors declare read/write scopes; the permission gate
  enforces them per call. Start with the father's Google workspace (Gmail,
  Drive, Calendar) — read-only first, writes behind the father's approval.
